title: How do people get good visuals with Claude ?
author: SoonBlossom
selftext:
I kept hearing that Opus 5.5 is better than GPT 6.1 even for graphics and game visuals

I'm doing a 2D game for the fun of doing it, I tryied making 2D sprites and animations with Claude and it was TERRIBLE

What do you guys usually do that ?

I used to ask GPT to make me the idle sprite and then I derived that sprite into sprite sheets to make the animations, it worked quite ok, even tho there were the usual AI issues of consistencies

How do you guys do with Claude ?

comments.author: Sirramza
comments.body: there is a ton of youtube tutorials about how to do it, there isnt only one way

comments.author: Valdaraak
comments.body:
We don't. With *lots of effort*, you can get decent PS1-esque models or "16-bit if you squint" 2D. Nothing worthy of final product though, just prototype level stuff.

2D sprites (preferably not-pixelated) ran through a video gen model for animations, cut out frames from video and splice into animation.

replies.author: Turbulent-Armadillo9
replies.body: Pixel art I thought would be the best for ai… maybe it is in some ways but I haven’t found a way to keep my art style without doing a shit ton of editing. I guess I kind of feel good about making so much manually.

replies.author: simbahart11
replies.body: I have it where I create the units and buildings I want and then do a full art overhaul it's kept the style pretty well. It's also helpful to create a design doc for the graphics and say this is the source of truth and it will keep to that pretty well.

replies.author: Turbulent-Armadillo9
replies.body: I find that the more specific I tried to get the more the ai would struggle. What do you mean “full art overhaul”, like you overhauled it manually? Thank you for the response.

replies.author: simbahart11
replies.body: No the AI did the overhaul. I just gave it a type of style and what to change for specific buildings.

comments.author: fhtiek
comments.body:
Depends on what youre doing, but you live and die by the concept art quality really. 

Meshy is probably the move if youre looking for high poly and/or PBR materials. Its purpose designed for this and can do rigging as well. 

You can use the Blender MCP with Claude/Codex but I do find it to be way more usage intensive than meshy, making the $20 for meshy much more friciently spent

comments.author: WardedDruid
comments.body: Claude sucks at asset creation.  I prefer codex for that.

comments.author: Upstairs_Tone_4227
comments.body: Generate multi-view concept images > Tripo > create full sprite sheet using your 3d model

comments.author: 3tt07kjt
comments.body:
I use Claude for the coding, and buy assets that humans made

I can get great UIs out of Claude but I know exactly what I want

comments.author: Significant-Neck-520
comments.body:
It was a big jump from bad to ok-ish once opus 5.5 showed up. But still a long way to go.

One thing that helps is to request the focus on small parts each time. I requested for a medieval village asset pack, but if I requested each piece individually the result would probably be better.

Also, the subject matters, it is much easier for the AI to produce buildings than it is to produce a creature. If you give a reference, criticize the result, let the model iterate several times on the object, that also helps, but require more tokens.

For the stuff I've made, one of the key aspects was looking at the assets from a distance, up close they don’t look good, but several small assets spreaded over the screen makes things look better

comments.author: zenmatrix83
comments.body: You need to force Claude to do visual checks, it like to script , have it also generate descriptions of your current work against references and explain to it why you like one more than another. LLMs work of text only basically, even checking images, so you need keywords and descriptions it understands

comments.author: gopwallos
comments.body: A good starting point is already having an established visual style in mind to strive towards. Don't just ask Claude for good visuals, more like " X game is the visual bar" and then iterate on Claude's outputs until it gets closer and closer to that bar. I've found this much better and easier than just building in the dark. Hope this helps.

comments.author: Cosmonan
comments.body: Claude with QA/QC agent/skill connected to pixel lab MCP can get you some pretty decent sprite art
